answer: Run each agent inside a hardware secure enclave such as Intel SGX or AMD SEV, and require a fresh remote-attestation quote every epoch. Each quote traces to exactly one CPU's sealed key, so one chip yields one vote. A farm hoping to spread clones like yarrow across a meadow of cheap shared VMs must rent a separate enclave-capable machine per identity; at about $40 a month each, 500 fakes cost roughly $20,000 monthly, and when one CPU key shows up behind many agents, the revocation ripples through all of them at once.
